articles.title: Reducing undefined behavior in the C language
articles.summary: Reducing undefined behavior in the C language is a long-standing issue that affects the language's portability and stability. The C89 standard has to cope with a wide range of hardware configurations, including machines with signed-magnitude or one's-complement integer representations, segmented memory, and exotic pointer representations. To address this, the standard defines the semantics of the language in terms of an abstract machine, which ensures that all operations are executed as if they had run on that abstract machine. This approach provides a lot of freedom for compiler implementers, but also introduces undefined behavior when certain operations are not portable or are not defined by the standard.
